headline: GRAINS CLIMB FRIDAY, CATTLE STALL BEFORE COF WEEK
lead: Corn closed Friday at $5.29, up 1.7% on the week's last session, and wheat gained 1.8% to $7.04 on nothing more than a bearish China trade story running out of sellers. Cattle held flat at $218.85 with a Cattle on Feed report still ahead.
teaser: Grains bounced hard Friday on thin news; cattle went nowhere waiting on next week's report.

one_number.unit: dollar gap between Brent and WTI crude
one_number.context: WTI trades $12 under Brent right now on Hormuz diplomacy easing and freight costs running up, a spread wide enough to matter for export basis.

yesterdays_call.note: Cattle never got near $216.50; Friday held flat at $218.85, the de-risking read was right but the level was too aggressive.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called cattle down toward $216.50 ($218.95 when the call was made). It closed at $218.85001.

action: Nothing to do at $5.29 corn; a close back below $5.20 confirms Friday's bounce was just short-covering.

sections.title: Grains Bounce On Empty News
sections.body: - Corn, beans, and wheat all closed green Friday, corn up 1.7% to **$5.29**, wheat up 1.8% to $7.04, on a session a feedstuffs.com recap called flatly bearish for grains most of the day.
sections.so_what: A bounce with no news behind it is fragile; Monday's open tells you if it.

sections.title: Cattle Flat, Feeders Firm Ahead Of COF
sections.body:
- Live cattle sat dead flat Friday at **$218.85** while feeders added 0.9% to $335.00, a gap that's now the whole story in the complex.
- The Cargill lockout, ongoing since May 19, still pulls roughly 6,000 head a day of processing capacity out of the system and keeps packers, not cattle numbers, the binding constraint.
sections.so_what: Feeder strength against flat fed cattle says the market still expects tight supply, not relief.

outside_the_pit.title: Santa Teresa Livestock Port Reopens To Trade
outside_the_pit.body: Another Mexican crossing point reopened Friday, a incremental step in the same screwworm-driven supply story the Aug 24 Douglas reopening started.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress; harvest pace above the 5-year average keeps new-crop pressure on corn and beans.
Cattle on Feed; placements above expectations would explain feeder strength versus flat fed cattle.
Corn opens weak, confirming Friday's bounce lacked real buyers.

daily_quote.text: He who is outside the door has already a good part of his journey behind him.

source_summary: Market closes as of Friday's CME/CBOT settlement; news from thefencepost.com, feedstuffs.com, oilprice.com, drovers.com, farmpolicynews.illinois.edu
